summary: Correct Phase 4 same-pool rejoin recovery: retain old-pool VM-delete tombstones and safely consume signed eject-cleanup provenance for shared resources. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: Same-pool rejoin no longer requires an operator to remove and add the affected shared resources again.

api.reason: Existing pool reconciliation and VM inventory operations keep their wire shapes; Core corrects durable rejoin results.

roadmap.reason: The fixes do not close Phase 4 or its recovery gates; native clean replay remains outstanding.

state.reason: Core owns VM-delete history, managed resource lifecycle and eject-cleanup provenance; Controller adopts the resulting Core inventory.
state.record: The member's Core managed journal stores signed eject-cleanup provenance and its one-time consumption receipt. pool-vms.json retains an old-pool vm-delete tombstone; the pool master adopts it from the rejoined member's current inventory and prunes only the matching stale owner record.

verification.method: Reported focused, package and race checks were independently reviewed. A reset native final campaign passed retained-local eject after fresh target inventory, solo-pool deletion, same-ID Controller-driven rejoin, and original shared network/repository/ISO ID reapplication. It does not establish old-pool tombstone pruning or Phase 4 acceptance.
